label: Tower value separation
query: How should Tower separate value-at-stake, committed value, measuring value, and realized savings for the Kyriba program?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings’ Kyriba program, Tower should treat value as a funnel: (1) value-at-stake at Strategy, (2) committed value at BAFO / Executive Decision, (3) measurement-ready value as part of Transition design, and (4) realized savings only when Treasury P&L and cash metrics show it. Each layer needs its own owner, artifact, and evidence. Why Your Kyriba Source spine (LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026) is approved through Strategy → BAFO, but Executive Decision, Selection, Transition, and Value are still “needs review”. That means you already have a top-down value thesis but not a signed-off value contract or measurement design. Tower’s job is to prevent leakage between “what a deck says” and “what shows up in cash / earnings” — which is exactly the risk zone between BAFO and post-go‑live for Kyriba. As Azure private-plane and data inventory are already stood up for Intelligence, you have the telemetry substrate to wire Tower into real transaction and working-capital data instead of staying at PowerPoint. Decision fork Option A: Treat Kyriba as the flagship value taxonomy pattern for Tower and over-build the four value layers now — slower, but reusable across future finance moves. Option B: Do a thinner Kyriba pass focused only on a couple of headline metrics (e.g., interest expense and idle cash), faster but less reusable.
